instrumental cause linking to next verse

items.question: How does reflection on the fear of existence arise in the heart?
premises: Fear of worldly existence can produce a touch or contact in the heart.
From that contact, reflection on the fear of existence can arise.
This manifest reflection ultimately occurs through the descent of power.
items.inference: Even a fear-born touch in the heart becomes a manifest reflection on existential fear because it is activated by the descent of power.
uncertainties: The exact nuance of ādrava as touch, melting, or agitation is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Even from a touch born of fear of worldly existence, a reflection on the fear of existence arises and becomes manifest in the heart through the descent of power.

rows.grounds: description of those in whom he is manifest

items.question: In whom does Bhairava become manifest through the transcendence of time?
premises: Some practitioners dry up the time principle that drives the stars.
Their minds delight in the absorption that devours time.
Bhairava becomes manifest in such minds.
items.inference: Bhairava is manifest in those whose contemplative absorption transcends and consumes the limiting power of time.
uncertainties: The compound nakṣatraprerakakālatattva can be parsed in slightly different ways, but the sense of transcending time remains clear.
items.plain_english: He is manifest in those who dry up the time principle that drives the stars, and in minds that delight in the absorption which devours time.

rows.grounds: extends the scope to other goddess groups

items.question: Whose roaring sound terrifies contracted bound beings?
premises: The goddesses of one's own senses produce a roaring sound.
The fourfold group of Khecari and others, within and without, also participates in this.
This roaring sound instills fear in contracted bound beings.
items.inference: The terrifying roar arises from the goddesses of the senses and the inner and outer groups such as Khecari, affecting bound beings.
uncertainties: The exact grouping of the fourfold khecari class is assumed from standard Tantric taxonomy.
items.plain_english: The roaring sound of the goddesses of one's own senses, and also of the fourfold group of Khecari and others within and without, is for the fear of contracted bound beings.

rows.grounds: refers to the group mentioned before

items.question: Why is the deity praised as Bhairava in the scripture?
premises: He is the lord of the goddess groups described earlier.
He is greatly terrifying because he shatters the course of worldly existence.
Teachers praise him in scripture through such etymological meanings.
items.inference: The name Bhairava is explained theologically as the lord who is terrifying in breaking the cycle of worldly existence.
items.plain_english: As the lord of that group, greatly terrifying in shattering the course of worldly existence, he is praised in the scripture by the teachers with these etymological meanings as Bhairava.

items.question: What are play and independence in the context of Bhairava's nature?
premises: Divine play occurs where there is no concern with what should be rejected or accepted.
Play is the overflowing of the density of one's own bliss.
Independence is the will to abide in supremacy over all.
items.inference: Bhairava's play and independence are expressions of blissful sovereignty beyond dualistic valuation.
items.plain_english: Play is the overflowing of the density of one's own bliss in the absence of any talk of what is to be rejected or accepted; likewise, independence is the will to abide in supremacy over all.

rows.grounds: definition related to mantra or speech

items.question: How are articulate expression and praise understood in Bhairava's undivided self?
premises: Even in the undivided self, activity can appear through difference.
Such differentiated expression is called articulate expression.
Because everything is manifested, that shining forth is called praise.
items.inference: Expression and praise are modes in which the undivided reality manifests difference and illumination without losing its unity.
uncertainties: saṃjalpa may also carry a nuance of inner discourse or mantra-like formulation.
items.plain_english: Articulate expression is activity through difference even within the undivided self, and because everything is manifested, that illumination is called praise.

items.question: What is the nature of the path after the attainment of the self?
premises: From the attainment of the self onward, one becomes inclined toward that reality.
This orientation applies in every action to be done.
The path is awareness, all action, and the qualities of seeing and doing.
items.inference: After self-attainment, the path integrates awareness and action in every deed through the powers of knowing and doing.
items.plain_english: From the attainment of the self onward, in every action to be done, the path is inclined toward that reality; it consists of awareness, consists of all action, and has the qualities of seeing and doing.

items.question: Why is the deity called Pati and identified as wholly auspicious Shiva?
premises: Teachers explain the deity through etymologies in the scripture on the body of Shiva.
He commands, restrains, protects, and matures, thereby benefiting all.
Because of these functions he is called Pati, and in him there is nothing inauspicious.
items.inference: The lordship of Shiva is defined by beneficent governance, so his nature is entirely auspicious.
uncertainties: The compound śāsanarodhanapālanapācanayoga compresses several functions traditionally associated with the term Pati.
items.plain_english: Thus, by etymological explanations in the scripture on the body of Shiva, the teachers have taught the god: because he commands, restrains, protects, and matures, he benefits all. Therefore he is Pati, and Shiva is indeed wholly auspicious; there is nothing inauspicious in him.

items.question: Why is the qualifier 'supreme and great' applied to Shiva's state?
premises: A little of such a form may shine in Rudra, Upendra, and others.
Shiva removes limitation rather than being limited by it.
Therefore the qualifier 'supreme and great state' is applied to him.
items.inference: Because Shiva transcends the partial manifestations found in other deities, he is designated by the supreme and great state.
uncertainties: The sandhi in tenāvacchedanude is compressed; the sense of removing limitation is inferred from context.
items.plain_english: Since even a little of such a form may shine in Rudra, Upendra, and others, the qualifier 'supreme and great state' is applied to him as the one who removes limitation.

items.question: By what authority and method is the knowable reality being shown?
premises: The true reality to be known is being shown.
It is shown by the command of Shiva.
The exposition proceeds through one's own awareness, true reasoning, lordly scripture, and the Trika sequence.
items.inference: The teaching of ultimate reality is grounded in Shiva's command and articulated through awareness, reasoning, scripture, and Trika tradition.
uncertainties: The compound patiśāstra may refer to authoritative scripture or to the doctrine of the Lord; the broader sense is clear.
items.plain_english: Thus, that true reality which is to be known is shown by me, by the command of Shiva, through my own awareness, sound reasoning, the lordly scripture, and the sequence of the Trika.

items.question: How do Shiva's three primary powers become twelve?
premises: Shiva has three powers beginning with Para.
These powers shine in creation, maintenance, dissolution, and the fourth state.
Operating across these four domains, they are declared as twelve.
items.inference: The three primary powers unfold into twelve by functioning in the four cosmic domains.
items.plain_english: His three powers, beginning with Para, shine in creation, maintenance, dissolution, and the fourth state; therefore they are declared as twelve.

items.question: Where do worshippers become fully established in relation to supreme Shiva?
premises: Supreme Shiva is called full in nature to that extent.
His fullness is understood through these powers.
Worshippers become directly and fully established right there.
items.inference: Direct establishment in supreme Shiva occurs in the very fullness expressed through his powers.
items.plain_english: To that extent this supreme Shiva is called of full nature; therefore worshippers are directly and fully established right there.

items.question: What explains the further divisions among Shiva's powers in the scriptures?
premises: The powers are further divided into portions of lesser, greater, and other arrangements.
These arrangements are explained in the scriptures.
Their cause is the force of Shiva's independence.
items.inference: All scriptural differentiations of the powers arise from Shiva's own sovereign freedom.
items.plain_english: The further arrangement of their divisions and portions, by lesser, greater, and so on, has been explained in the scriptures precisely by the force of his independence.

items.question: What are the first series of forms in which Bhairava is enumerated?
premises: Bhairava is described through successive numerical forms.
These forms range from one to eight in this verse.
Each form names a distinct configuration of his nature.
items.inference: Bhairava is presented as a single reality unfolding through multiple numerical configurations.
items.plain_english: He is the One Hero, then the Paired One, the one with three powers and fourfold nature, the one with five forms, the one with sixfold nature, and the one adorned as sevenfold and eightfold.

items.question: How does the enumeration of Bhairava's forms culminate in the twelvefold wheel?
premises: The enumeration continues beyond the eightfold forms.
Bhairava is described as ninefold, ten-directional, and elevenfold.
He culminates as lord of the great twelve-spoked wheel.
items.inference: The numerical unfolding of Bhairava reaches a culminating form as sovereign of the twelvefold wheel.
items.plain_english: Thus Bhairava is the ninefold self, the one with the powers of the ten directions and elevenfold nature, and the lord of the great twelve-spoked wheel.

items.question: How far does Bhairava's expansion extend in the cosmic wheel?
premises: Bhairava's forms can be enumerated up to a thousand spokes.
They can also extend to an uncountable number of spokes.
As universal power, the great lord expands in the wheel of the universe.
items.inference: Bhairava's manifestation is not limited to fixed numerical forms but expands infinitely as universal power.
items.plain_english: Thus, up to the thousand-spoked or even the uncountably spoked wheel of the universe, the lord, the great sovereign, expands as the power of the universe.

items.question: How are divisions among the many wheels explained without losing unity?
premises: There are many wheels of manifestation.
Each follows its own group or class.
Their divisions are determined through a unity that belongs to each wheel.
items.inference: Multiplicity among the wheels is organized by class-based unity rather than by absolute separation.
items.plain_english: Even among those wheels, divisions belonging to each wheel have been determined there by a unity that follows its own group.

rows.grounds: numerical basis in a specific tradition

items.question: How does the Traiśirasa doctrine explain the lordship over six wheels?
premises: The Traiśirasa doctrine uses a numerical combination of four, six, two, and two.
On that basis it states the lordship of the deity over six wheels.
This lord is described as having a wondrous own form.
items.inference: A specific scriptural tradition derives sixfold wheel-lordship from its own numerical scheme.
uncertainties: The internal arithmetic of the compound catuṣṣaḍdvirdvigaṇanā is compressed and tradition-specific.
items.plain_english: In the Traiśirasa doctrine, by the combination of counting four, six, two, and two, the lordship of the Lord, whose own form is wondrous, over six wheels has been stated.

items.question: How are the names of the wheel-goddesses determined in that system?
premises: The wheel-goddesses have distinct names.
Their names correspond to differences in function.
They are also formed etymologically through meditation on gentle and fierce forms of yoginis.
items.inference: The names of the wheel-goddesses express both their functions and the contemplative forms through which they are known.
items.plain_english: There, the names of the goddesses of the wheel are determined according to differences of function and by etymological formulation of the yoginis through meditation on their gentle and fierce forms.

rows.grounds: refers to the single lord of awareness

items.question: What is worshipped as the wheel of waves of awareness?
premises: The one lord of awareness has an inner creative intuition as his body-form.
That form may appear as gentle or as another measured manifestation.
This is worshipped as the wheel of waves of awareness.
items.inference: The wheel of awareness is the inner intuitive manifestation of the one lord, appearing in varied forms.
uncertainties: anyanmitaṃ could suggest a limited or differently measured form; the contrast with gentle is clear.
items.plain_english: The inner creative intuition of the one lord of awareness is his body-form; whether gentle or another measured form, it is worshipped as the wheel of waves of awareness.

rows.grounds: refers to the practitioner or lord

items.question: How is the goddess Awareness nourished in practice?
premises: The intention arises that this awareness should be nourished.
Nourishment comes from meditation mixed with articulate expression.
It also comes from external activity.
items.inference: Awareness is nourished through a combination of contemplative meditation, expressive formulation, and outward action.
items.plain_english: With the intention, 'May this be nourished,' the goddess Awareness is nourished by the meditation described above mixed with articulate expression, and also by outward activity.

items.question: What is the effect when nourished awareness becomes clear?
premises: When nourished, awareness becomes clear and shines.
That clear awareness grants a corresponding fruit to the practitioner.
Nourishment is like a dry place becoming a lake through clear water.
items.inference: Clarified awareness yields fitting results, transforming dryness into fullness like water forming a lake.
uncertainties: sitam can mean white or clear; in the water analogy, clear fits best.
items.plain_english: When it becomes clear, awareness shines and grants a corresponding fruit to him. Nourishment is like a dry place becoming a lake, and for that clear water is needed.

items.question: How do naturally essence-flowing sounds support meditation centered on awareness?
premises: Meditation centered on that awareness is extended by following it.
Certain sounds or letters are by nature flowing with essence.
These sounds serve as examples of what supports the practice.
items.inference: Meditation on awareness is strengthened by aligning with sounds whose intrinsic nature carries nourishing essence.
uncertainties: rasa may suggest fluid, savor, or essence; essence fits the nourishing context.
items.plain_english: Therefore, by following that, meditation centered on it is extended; and there are sounds which by their own nature flow with essence, as follows.

items.question: How do certain phonetic combinations clarify awareness?
premises: Certain sounds are mostly dental, labial, and dental in character.
When formed together with certain other sounds, they attain a seed state.
In that seed state they make awareness clear.
items.inference: Specific phonetic combinations become potent seeds that clarify awareness.
uncertainties: The exact mantra or syllables intended by the phonetic description are not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Those sounds, mostly dental, labial, and dental, formed together with certain other sounds, attain the state of a seed and make that awareness clear.
